findings.evidence: template/scripts/lifecycle_overview.py: observe_candidate catches `(queue.QueueError, MalformedMarkerError, ValueError)`. overview() runs `list(pool.map(lambda pr: observe_candidate(...), prs))`. main() catches only `(OverviewError, QueueError)`.
findings.summary: observe_candidate only converts QueueError, MalformedMarkerError and ValueError into an `unknown` item. Any other exception in a worker thread (for example KeyError on a malformed PR payload, or an OSError from a gh call) propagates through pool.map and aborts the whole summary. The spec says an unreadable source should make that item `unknown`, not fail the report.

findings.evidence: lifecycle_overview.py: `reason.startswith("malformed marker")`, `reason.startswith(("claim recorded on earlier head", "checks do not match candidate head"))`, `reason.startswith("post-merge") and "exhausted" in reason`. The matching producer strings are in candidate_lifecycle.py lines 264, 331, 438 and 525. They are not shared constants.
findings.summary: The overview detects `stale-head`, `post-merge-exhausted` and `unknown-source` (malformed marker) by matching free-text prefixes of `candidate['reason']`. The prefixes currently match candidate_lifecycle.py. If the derivation wording changes, these exceptions silently stop being reported, and the item could be classified `delivering` or `blocked` without the named finding.
